mārūtum: sonship, the status of a son (from mārum “son”), here adoption as a son: ana mārūtim (ma-ru-tim) “as a son”, literally “into sonship”; with the suffix, mārūtišu (ma-ru-ti-šu) “his sonship”: ša ana mārūtišu ilqûšuma “whom he took as his son, and” · noun
tarbītum: a foster-child, one who is brought up (from the D-stem of rabûm “to bring up”, tarbītum “what is raised”): tarbītum (tar-bi-tum, nominative), tarbītim (tar-bi-tim, genitive after ana): ana tarbītim ilqēma “he took (him) as a foster-child, and”; the same child as mārūtum seen from the side of the one raised · noun
ummiānum: a craftsman, a skilled worker (written with the Sumerograms UM.MI.A, three signs UM, MI, A, with no ending written): ummiānim “of a craftsman” (genitive, read from the context); mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, literally “a son of a craftsman” (see mārum) · noun, Sumerogram
NER.SE.GA: NER.SE.GA (the signs KIŠ, ŠE and GA) — a class of person whose son is named beside the zikrum class and the palace servant (“the son of a NER.SE.GA”); given as the signs only, with no reading and no translation, UNCERTAIN (the middle sign could be another sign than ŠE) · Sumerogram, untranslated
ḫiāṭum: UNCERTAIN verb, the root not settled; read from the context as “to look out for, to seek out”: iḫīaṭ (i-ḫi-a-aṭ) “he looked for (?)”, said of seeking a father and mother; who the subject is, the man or the child, is also UNCERTAIN · verb
rēqum: empty (the adjective): rīqūssu (ri-qu₂-zu) “empty-handed (?)”, a reading from the signs RI + QU + ZU, probably rīqūtum “emptiness” + -šu (t + š said ss, spelled with ZU), used as an adverb; Harper prints tal-ku-zu; the form and the sense “empty-handed” are both UNCERTAIN · adjective / adverb (uncertain)
edûm-D: UNCERTAIN verb, read as the D-stem of edûm “to know”: “to make known, to identify, to point out”: uwaddīma (u-wi-id-di-ma) “he has identified (?), and”, D-stem + -ma; the form and the sense are UNCERTAIN · D-stem verb
ṣiārum: UNCERTAIN verb, the root not settled (perhaps a hollow verb ṣiārum); read from the context as “to turn away from, to leave”: iṣīrma (i-ṣi-ir-ma) “he has turned away from (?), and”, with -ma; the sense follows the sequence of the law · verb
atta: you (the independent pronoun of the second person): atta (at-ta) masculine “you (m.)”, atti (at-ti) feminine “you (f.)”: ul abī atta, ul ummī atti “you are not my father, you are not my mother” · pronoun
lišānum: tongue (written EME, the sign KA × ME, in Harper’s list the word lišānu): lišānšu (EME-šu) “his tongue”, with -šu · noun, Sumerogram
mušēniqtum: wet-nurse, one who gives a child suck (the feminine Š-stem participle of enēqum “to suck”, built from the form; not found in an earlier part): mušēniqtim (mu-še-ni-iq-tim, genitive), mušēniqtum (mu-še-ni-iq-tum, nominative) · noun
rakāsum: to bind; with a child, to bind oneself to, to take on (UNCERTAIN in this use): irtakas (ir-ta-ka-aš) “she has bound”, perfect, said of taking on a child; irkusu (ir-ku-šu) “(because) she bound”, preterite with the subjunctive -u, the last sign written ŠU, read as the ending su · verb, G-stem
tulûm: breast (written UBUR, Harper’s list no. 105 tulû; the identification of the character is tentative): tulêša (UBUR-ša) “her breast”, with -ša; the form tulê looks plural (UNCERTAIN), the sense “breast” being singular in the law · noun, Sumerogram

__broaden__.mû: water(s); mê nuḫšim “waters of abundance” · ina mêšu (ME-e-šu) “in his waters”, of a child taken while in the waters of birth, i.e. perhaps a newborn, the idiom UNCERTAIN; the form mê is the oblique of a plural-looking noun
__broaden__.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma) · ilqi (il-qi₂) “he took”; ilqûšu (il-qu₂-u-šu) “(when) he took him”, with the subjunctive -u and -šu “him”; ilqûšuma (il-qu₂-šu-ma) “he took him, and” (with the subjunctive -u before -šu, after ša); ana tarbītim ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took (him) as a foster-child, and”
__broaden__.rabûm-D: D-stem of rabûm: to bring up, raise: urabbāšu “she shall raise him” · urabba (present) “he shall raise (the orchard)” · urabbû (u-ra-ab-bu-u) “they shall bring up” (present plural), with young children as object · urtabbišu (ur-ta-ab-bi-šu) “he has raised him”, perfect + -šu; urabbûšu (u-ra-ab-bu-šu, also u-ra-ab-bu-u-šu) “(whom) he raised”, the preterite urabbi + the subjunctive -u (said û) + -šu “him”; murabbīšu (mu-ra-bi-šu) “the one who raised him”, murabbītišu (mu-ra-bi-ti-šu) “the one (f.) who raised him”, murabbīssu (mu-ra-bi-zu) “his raiser”: participles of the D-stem with the suffix, said of the foster-father and foster-mother
__broaden__.baqārum-N: N-stem of baqārum (Harper BAKARU IV): to be claimed: ibbaqqar (ib-ba-qar, present) “he shall be claimed”, ul ibbaqqar “no claim shall be made” · ul ibbaqqar written ib-ba-aq-qar (with the sign AK read aq) and ib-ba-qar: “no claim shall be made”, said of the foster-child
__broaden__.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone · bīssu (É-ba(=zu): the plate sign is BA where ZU is meant) “his house”, the t of bītum and -šu said ss: bīssu ipuš “he has set up a house of his own”; bīt abišu “his father’s house” (É a-bi-šu), bīt written É alone
__broaden__.târum: to return: ul itârma “he shall never again …” · itâr (i-ta-ar) “he shall go back”: ana bīt abišu itâr “he shall go back to his father’s house”
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son” · mārī (DUMU-i) “my son” (-ī “my”); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “children” in mārī ūlissum “children she bore him”; mārū (DUMU{meš}) “sons” as subject: mārū ana ummātim ul izuzzū “the sons shall not divide by mothers” · mār X (DUMU, the sign TUR) “a member of the class X”, literally “son of X”: mār ummiānim “a craftsman”, mār zinništim “the son of a woman”; māram (DUMU) “a son”, mārašu (DUMU-šu) “his son”, mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons”, mārīšu “his sons”
__broaden__.izuzzum: to stand; izzazzu “he stands (in service)” · izzaz, izzazma (i-za-az, i-za-az-ma) “she shall stand (take her place)”, of an heir’s share: zittam kīma aplim ištēn izzazma “she shall take a share like one heir, and”; ul izzaz “she shall have no share”; sense UNCERTAIN · mūzaz (mu-za-az) “one who stands (in service)”, the participle, construct before a genitive: mūzaz ekallim “one who stands in the palace’s service”
__broaden__.ekallum: palace (É.GAL “great house”) — the crown as owner · ekallim (É.GAL, two signs with no ending written) “of the palace”, genitive after mūzaz
__broaden__.zikrum-class: zikrum (zi-ik-ru-um) — the name of a class of woman, named beside the ugbabtum (NIN.AN) in §178–179 and beside the kallātim in §180; it is not zikrum “name” of the prologue, and what the class was is not known, UNCERTAIN · noun · zikrum also in mār zinništim zikrum “the son of a woman, a zikrum”, still UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take” · itti mārīšu “among his sons” (it-ti, written IT, the sign A₂, and TI): the sense “among, in the number of”, after manûm “to count”
__broaden__.šiprum: work, labour: šiprim “of work” · šipir (ši-pi₂-ir) construct “the work of”: šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands”, the craft taught to a son
__broaden__.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands”
__broaden__.aḫāzum-Š: Š-stem of aḫāzum “to take”: to make take, have (a man) take (a wife): ušaḫḫazūšu (u-ša-aḫ-ḫa-zu-šu) “they shall have him take (a wife)” (present plural + -šu “him”) · uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him”, Š-stem perfect with -šu “him”, the z of the stem and š said ss, spelled with ZU: šipir qātīšu uštāḫissu “he has taught him the work of his hands”; the Š-stem here is “to make learn”
__broaden__.manûm-count: to count, reckon (the verb; the noun manûm “mina” is another word): imannû(ma) “they shall count” — 3rd plural, impersonal · imtanûšu (im-ta-nu-šu) “he has counted him”, perfect with -šu “him” and a -u- written before it: itti mārīšu lā imtanûšu “he has not counted him among his sons”
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house) · ipuš (i-pu-uš, the sign BU read pu) “he made”: bīssu ipuš “he made his house”, i.e. set up a house of his own (preterite)
__broaden__.nasāḫum: to pull out, uproot; of a son, to cast out, disinherit (Harper: “to cut off, to disinherit”): nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im, infinitive) “to cast out”; anassaḫ (a-na-za-aḫ) “I shall cast out” (first person present); inassaḫ (i-na-za-aḫ) “he shall cast out” (third person present) · inassaḫū (i-na-za-ḫu) “they shall pluck out”, present plural: īnšu inassaḫū “they shall pluck out his eye” (the ZA sign for sa) · nasāḫim (na-sa-ḫi-im) infinitive “to cast out”: ana tarbītim nasāḫim “to cast out the foster-child”
__broaden__.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast”
__broaden__.kânum-D: D-stem of kânum: to convict, prove against someone (uktīn, ukannūšuma) · uktīn (uk-ti-in, perfect, with the infixed -t-) “he has convicted”; ukannūšuma (u-ka-an-nu-šu-ma, present, plural, with -šu “him” and -ma) “they shall convict him, and”; ukānma (u-ka-an-ma, present, singular) “he shall convict, and” · ukannūšima (u-ka-an-nu-ši-ma) “they shall convict her, and”, present plural with -ši “her” and -ma
__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye” · after a t, on a verb: uštāḫissu (uš-ta-ḫi-zu) “he has taught him” (the z of the stem + -šu said ss, spelled ZU); on nouns bīssu (É-ba/zu) “his house” and the participles murabbīšu, murabbītišu, murabbīssu “the one who raised him”; on a verb, ilqûšu, urtabbišu, urabbûšu, imtanûšu “him”; on the noun lišānšu (EME-šu) “his tongue”, īnšu “his eye”, mêšu “his waters”, mārūtišu “his sonship”
